description:
About the Position

This is a fully funded PhD studentship in Dr Dominique Laniel's research group at the School of Physics and Astronomy, investigating the chemistry of lanthanide and actinide metals and oxides under extreme conditions. This PhD opening at The University of Edinburgh centres on Extreme Conditions Chemistry of Lanthanide and Actinide Metals at University of Edinburgh. Disciplinary scope: Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science. The role is based in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. Full funding is provided; financial support is listed as 3.5-4/year. Timing: Open all year - Rolling basis.

Research Focus

  • High-Pressure Chemistry: Behavior of lanthanide and actinide compounds under extreme pressures
  • Synthesis of Novel Materials: Creating new compounds with unique properties
  • Crystallography: Determining structures of high-pressure phases
  • Electronic Properties: Investigating electronic behavior under compression
  • Nuclear Materials: Understanding materials relevant to nuclear energy

Funding & Benefits

  • Tuition Fees: Full coverage (UK/EU rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Stipend: £21,805 (2026/27 UKRI minimum) per year (UKRI rate) for 3.5-4 years
  • Research Costs: Access to high-pressure facilities and synchrotron sources
  • Travel: Funding for international conferences and experiments

Eligibility and Requirements

  • Strong undergraduate degree in Physics, Chemistry, Materials Science, or related field
  • Interest in extreme conditions research
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Willingness to work at international facilities
  • Residency: UK/EU students

Application Process

  1. Contact supervisor
  2. Discuss research interests
  3. Submit application through university system
  4. Provide academic documents
  5. Interview process
  6. Award notification

About the University of Edinburgh

University of Edinburgh is a public research university in Scotland's capital and a member of the Russell Group. It offers undergraduate, postgraduate and doctoral programmes across medicine, science, engineering, humanities and social sciences. Its research community supports collaboration across disciplines, connecting academic inquiry with challenges affecting health, technology and society.

Official website: https://www.ed.ac.uk/

  • Research applicable to nuclear energy and waste management.

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: Open all year - Rolling basis. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
